verdict.rationale: Flagsmith's Release Pipelines are a first-party rule engine: you define stages with triggers and actions that automatically advance flag rollouts, and promoting a flag to production can auto-generate change requests. The scope is limited to flag-release progression, and the evidence never says which events can act as triggers. Scheduled flags are time-based one-off changes, and audit-log webhooks are outbound streaming, so neither counts as event-driven rules. Missing for 10: documented trigger/event types and conditions, general-purpose event-to-action rules beyond release pipelines, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Define stages that your flags progress through automatically, with triggers and actions that control rollouts to selected environments and audiences.
Release Pipelines can automatically generate change requests when promoting flags to production, eliminating manual effort and streamlining your deployment workflow.
Release Pipelines act as your intelligent release assistant, automating your entire feature flag deployment process.
